# 1 Enoch Chapter 95 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 95:1 — 'cloud of waters' lament — imagery

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Oh-that-mine-eyes-were a-cloud-of-waters" | Archaic; preserves the Ge'ez hyperbole literally |
| LOGOS | "Would that my eyes were a cloud of waters" | Formal optative; more natural |
| PNEUMA | "If only my eyes could become a raincloud" | 'Raincloud' clarifies; modern idiom |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Would that my eyes were a cloud of waters' is the correct optative and preserves the literal Ge'ez image. 'Raincloud' (PNEUMA) reduces the double 'cloud of waters' parallelism that is textually present.

---

## 95:1 — 'trouble of heart' vs. 'anguish of heart'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "trouble-of-heart" | Literal: hezán lebb — grief/trouble of heart |
| LOGOS | "anguish of heart" | 'Anguish' conveys emotional intensity |
| PNEUMA | "anguish in my heart" | Agrees with LOGOS on 'anguish' |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS 'anguish of heart.' 'Anguish' better conveys the Hebrew/Ge'ez hezán (grief, deep distress) than 'trouble.' The construct form 'of heart' (EMET/LOGOS) preferred over PNEUMA's 'in my heart.'

---

## 95:4 — 'fulminate anathemas' vs. 'pronounce anathemas'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "fulminate-anathemas which-cannot-be-reversed" | 'Fulminate' = archaic for 'pronounce with force' |
| LOGOS | "pronounce anathemas that cannot be reversed" | Formal; accessible |
| PNEUMA | "pronounce curses you cannot take back" | 'Curses' for 'anathemas'; informal |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Pronounce anathemas' preserves the technical religious-judicial term. 'Fulminate' (EMET) is unnecessarily archaic. PNEUMA's 'curses' loses the specific force of binding religious prohibition.

---

## 95:5 — 'requite' vs. 'repay'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "requite-your-neighbour with-evil" | 'Requite' = archaic for repay/return |
| LOGOS | "repay your neighbor with evil" | Standard modern English |
| PNEUMA | "pay back your neighbor with evil" | Colloquial; equally clear |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS 'repay.' Both LOGOS and PNEUMA are acceptable; LOGOS formal register preferred for consistency with the woe oracle series.

---

## 95:6 — 'weigh out injustice'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "those-who-weigh-out-injustice" | Literal: scales/balance metaphor for legal corruption |
| LOGOS | "those who weigh out injustice" | Formal; preserves scales metaphor |
| PNEUMA | "all who tip the scales toward injustice" | 'Tip the scales' is an English idiom for the same |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Weigh out injustice' preserves the Ge'ez commercial/judicial imagery precisely. PNEUMA's 'tip the scales' is a good English equivalent but naturalizes away the original metaphor.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 5**
